selection_basis: ZITADEL, Keycloak and authentik all passed the same frozen 20-step identity Stage A fixture; the incumbent failed 9 mandatory central identity-provider steps while its existing production guards still passed.

ZITADEL is selected for composition because machine identities are a direct primitive and it had the smallest measured two-component footprint and fastest complete destructive run among the service candidates; the owner-accepted AGPL service/API boundary remains explicit.
Keycloak is the fallback: equally clean service-account/OIDC semantics and Apache-2.0 licensing, with materially higher measured memory/startup cost in this LAB.
authentik is retained as a specialized reserve: core-only M2M semantics passed cleanly, but server+worker+PostgreSQL produced the broadest tested runtime surface and slowest startup.
next_gate: Run credential-broker destructive benchmark and scorecards, then execute cross-role composition with identity winner/fallback plus authorization and credential selections. No production authority before composition PASS and later promotion gate.
